protocol.warmup: same prompt + up to 4 decode steps, then reset; excluded from timing
protocol.eos: ignored for fixed-length throughput; output after first EOS is not a chat answer
protocol.decode_formula: (generated_ids - 1) / decode_seconds; first token belongs to prefill
protocol.prefill_formula: prompt_tokens / prefill_seconds; includes final vocabulary projection
notes: One process/configuration at a time, with an advisory local benchmark lock.
Round order alternates to reduce fixed-order bias; no thermal/power isolation.
Tokenizer, model load, shader compilation and warmup excluded from tokens/sec.
Full-model execution is hybrid CPU/Metal, not fully GPU-resident.
Exactness is against the existing quantized CPU engine, not an fp32 teacher model.

Unified memory on Apple Silicon, often referred to as the Unified Memory Interface (UMI), is a revolutionary architectural shift that fundamentally changes how machine learning models are trained. By eliminating the traditional separation between the CPU and GPU, this architecture allows the entire system to operate as a single, cohesive unit.

The primary benefit is the removal of the "memory bottleneck." In traditional setups, the CPU struggles to access GPU memory, causing the GPU to wait for data from the CPU, which slows down the entire training process. With UMI, the CPU and GPU share the same memory space, meaning the CPU can directly access the GPU's memory bandwidth
